    "Vitamin C dosage calculation based on body weight rather than body surface area may have led to different results.",
    "Rats are vitamin C-synthesizing species, whereas humans are not.",
    "Rats appear to poorly absorb vitamin C from the diet.",
    "Genetically variant strains incapable of synthesizing vitamin C do not fully recapitulate vitamin C metabolism or effects of depletion/repletion observed in humans.",
    "Guinea pigs may be a more appropriate model for studying in vivo effects of vitamin C supplementation.",
    "Laboratory rodents serving as controls are metabolically morbid and exhibit increased levels of inflammatory cytokines."

  "key_numbers": [
    "1/19 significant species × exercise interactions (catalase)",
    "10/19 significant species × vitamin C interactions",
    "Exercise increased oxidative stress and induced an inflammatory state in rats and humans.",
    "Vitamin C decreased oxidative stress and increased antioxidant capacity only in humans.",
    "Vitamin C induced an anti-inflammatory state only in rats.",
    "Exercise after vitamin C administration altered redox state only in humans.",
    "Inflammation biomarkers changed similarly after exercise combined with vitamin C in both rats and humans.",
    "Magnitude of all perturbations after exercise was similar (14% in rats and 16% in humans).",
    "Vitamin C plasma levels increased by 92% in humans vs. 41% in rats.",
    "Resting values of inflammatory molecules were considerably higher in rats compared to humans."
  ]
